lessons.title: Data Communications, Networks and Protocols

reasons: Slide emphasis

lessons.searchText: Data Communications, Networks and Protocols ডেটা কমিউনিকেশন, নেটওয়ার্ক ও প্রোটোকল Data communications = exchange of data between two devices via a transmission medium. Four fundamental characteristics: delivery, accuracy, timeliness, jitter (slide 2). Components of a data communication system (Figure 1.1) and data flow: simplex, half-duplex, full-duplex (Figure 1.2). Network criteria: performance (delay, throughput), reliability, security (slide 6). Categories: LAN, WAN, MAN (slide 15). Protocol elements: syntax, semantics, timing (slide 27).

lessons.title: Protocol Layering, the OSI Model and TCP/IP
lessons.titleBn: প্রোটোকল লেয়ারিং, OSI মডেল ও TCP/IP

reasons: Slide emphasis

topics: Protocol Layering, the OSI Model and TCP/IP
lessons.searchText: Protocol Layering, the OSI Model and TCP/IP প্রোটোকল লেয়ারিং, OSI মডেল ও TCP/IP Two principles of protocol layering: each layer performs two opposite tasks; objects under each layer at both sites are identical (slide 4). ISO is the organization; OSI is the model (slide 6). Physical: bits hop to hop; data link: frames hop to hop; network: packets source host to destination host; transport: message process to process (slides 9–18). Session: dialog control and synchronization; presentation: translation, compression, encryption; application: services to the user (slides 19–22). Why OSI did not replace TCP/IP: late arrival, incompletely defined layers, insufficient performance (slide 30).

We commonly use periodic analog signals and nonperiodic digital signals (slide 9). Sine wave properties: peak amplitude, frequency, phase. Phase describes the position of the waveform relative to time 0. Wavelength = propagation speed × period = propagation speed / frequency.

reasons: Slide emphasis

lessons.searchText: Transmission Impairment: Attenuation, Distortion, Noise ট্রান্সমিশন ইমপেয়ারমেন্ট What is sent is not what is received: attenuation, distortion, noise (slide 61). dB = 10 log10(P2/P1); losses and gains in dB are additive (slides 63–66). dBm = 10 log10 Pm with Pm in milliwatts (slide 67). Distortion: components travel at different speeds, causing phase differences (slide 69). Noise types: thermal, induced, crosstalk, impulse (slide 70).

Latency = propagation time + transmission time + queuing time + processing delay. The bandwidth-delay product defines the number of bits that can fill the link.

lessons.searchText: Multilevel Schemes, Block Coding, PCM and Delta Modulation ব্লক কোডিং, PCM ও ডেল্টা মডুলেশন mBnL: m data elements encoded as n signal elements with 2^m ≤ L^n (slide 27). Block coding (mB/nB) replaces each m-bit group with an n-bit group (slide 32). PCM: sampling, quantization, encoding (slide 43). Nyquist theorem: sampling rate ≥ 2 × highest frequency (slide 47). Quantization SNR_dB = 6.02 nb + 1.76 (slide 58).

reasons: Supporting concept for other topics

lessons.searchText: Transmission Modes: Parallel and Serial ট্রান্সমিশন মোড: প্যারালেল ও সিরিয়াল Parallel: multiple bits per clock tick; serial: one bit per clock tick (slide 66). Asynchronous: 1 start bit (0), one or more stop bits (1s), possible gaps between bytes (slide 70). Asynchronous at the byte level, but bits are still synchronized (slide 71). Synchronous: bits sent one after another with no start/stop bits or gaps; receiver groups the bits (slide 73).

lessons.title: Multiplexing: FDM and WDM

reasons: Slide emphasis

lessons.searchText: Multiplexing: FDM and WDM মাল্টিপ্লেক্সিং: FDM ও WDM Multiplexing: simultaneous transmission of multiple signals across a single data link (slide 3). FDM is an analog technique, used when link bandwidth (Hz) exceeds the combined bandwidths of the signals (slide 7). Guard bands prevent overlapping; n channels need n − 1 guard bands (slides 9, 15). WDM is an analog multiplexing technique for optical signals, using prisms (slides 22–23).

lessons.title: Time-Division Multiplexing

reasons: Slide emphasis

lessons.searchText: Time-Division Multiplexing টাইম-ডিভিশন মাল্টিপ্লেক্সিং TDM is a digital technique combining several low-rate channels into one high-rate one (slide 25). In synchronous TDM the link rate is n times faster and the unit duration n times shorter (slide 27). Frame duration equals the duration of an input unit (slide 29). Data rate management: multilevel, multislot, pulse stuffing (slide 42). Framing (synchronization) bits are overhead (slide 46).

lessons.searchText: Unguided Media: Radio Waves, Microwaves, Infrared আনগাইডেড মিডিয়া Unguided media transport electromagnetic waves without a physical conductor (slide 26). Radio waves: multicast (radio, TV, paging), penetrate walls, omnidirectional antennas (slide 31). Microwaves: unicast (cellular, satellite, WLAN), line-of-sight, directional antennas (slide 33). Infrared: short range in a closed area, line of sight (slide 35).

lessons.title: Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA)

reasons: Slide emphasis

lessons.searchText: Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) CDMA Each user has a unique chipping sequence (code); all share the same frequency. Encoder output Z(i,m) = d(i)·c(m); decoder correlates received chips with the code. Multiple senders’ signals add in the channel; the right code recovers each one.

lessons.searchText: IEEE 802.11 Wireless LAN IEEE 802.11 ওয়্যারলেস LAN Architecture: BSS, AP, ad hoc; channels in 2.4 GHz may overlap. Association with passive (beacon) or active (probe) scanning. MAC: CSMA/CA — no collision detection; DIFS, backoff, ACK after SIFS. RTS/CTS reservation; four address fields in the 802.11 frame.
